title: Leakage ladder: original 2021 protocol → leak-free
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: balanced accuracy drop L0 → L3 (means over 20 seeds)
interpretation: Each removed leak lowers balanced accuracy; at the patient-disjoint rung accuracy equals the always-COPD baseline while balanced accuracy stays above chance. The original protocol did not reach the paper's reported figure in this re-implementation.
limitations: Re-implementation of git 3ec7dc6 with authentic labels; batch size 32 assumed (not stated); released-code class sizes match the paper for Healthy/COPD/Pneumonia but are half for Bronchiectasis/Bronchiolitis (paper Fig. 1); model matches every layer of the paper's Fig. 3 (328,726 parameters; the figure's printed total 320,726 does not match its rows); COPD cap applied in sorted file order (original used os.listdir order).
decision: supports H1 (drop criterion met); reproduction criterion for L0 not met
justification: Pre-registered: drop L0→L3 ≥ 0.15 supports H1; |L0 − 0.9567| ≤ 0.03 for reproduction.

title: Site vs sample-rate/bandwidth diagnostic (round-2 served model)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: share of ICBHI COPD recordings predicted asthma at 4 kHz
interpretation: Re-encoding ICBHI audio in KAUH's 4 kHz format lowers accuracy somewhat but rarely yields 'asthma', unlike the external KAUH patients; bandwidth does not explain the failure.
limitations: Test + validation recordings of split v2 (validation was used for early stopping only; comparison is paired). Only 12 healthy ICBHI recordings. One 4 kHz recording was refused by the lung-sound gate (counted as gate_rejected).
decision: supports H2 over the bandwidth explanation
justification: Pre-registered in RESEARCH_PLAN H2.

title: Failed round-2b production run (OPERA-CE head-export check, TF32)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
interpretation: All three RespiNets and the YAMNet head trained; stopped at the OPERA-CE head check. With C = 0.1 the GPU (TF32) head differed from scikit-learn by up to 2.2e-3 (32 of 325 validation rows > 1e-3; no class changes); on the CPU the same head matched to 3.5e-6.
decision: root-cause fix (D-23): heads always run on the CPU (pretrained.predict_head), tolerance 1e-4; run repeated from a clean tree
justification: Kept for the record; no metrics. Same failure class as EXP-006, which was relaxed instead of fixed.

title: Superseded round-2b production artifact (served weights ≠ evaluated weights)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
interpretation: Test metrics, calibration and fusion temperatures were computed on EarlyStopping-restored weights (members seed43/44: epochs 50/42); the saved files the server loaded were the later ModelCheckpoint epochs 56/44. Its KAUH-holdout run (served file): 17/24 in-label patients, healthy 17/18, COPD 0/5. Deployment checks passed (parity 5e-5) but compared served files with themselves, so they could not detect this. Re-scoring all 389 test recordings through the served files on the GPU (the evaluation device): 1 recording differs (a healthy one; balanced accuracy 0.7427 vs reported 0.7507, accuracy 0.8226 vs 0.8252); patient-level metrics identical. On the CPU 2 recordings differ (one more from TF32). So the mismatch was real but changed one test recording (reported_metrics_reproduction*.json).
limitations: Not a valid estimate of any single model: metrics and served weights differ.
justification: Kept for the record; its test and holdout numbers are not reported as results.

title: Contamination re-evaluation: Kaggle-V2-trained models scored on all ICBHI recordings
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: within-model accuracy difference, copied − clean ICBHI COPD recordings (Kaggle-trained model)
interpretation: A model trained on Kaggle V2 scores ICBHI recordings that were copied into Kaggle far higher than clean ICBHI recordings of the same class; a model trained without the copies loses most of that advantage. A 'train on Kaggle V2, test on ICBHI' evaluation largely re-tests training audio.
limitations: Recording-level accuracy with patient-cluster bootstrap. Copied and clean recordings come from different patients and may differ systematically (selection by the uploader). The between-model comparison also changes the class set (5 → 4; no COPD without the copies) and the training size (715 → 338 recordings). One seed per model. Pneumonia: 6 patients.
justification: Mandatory control C4 (novelty review §7; D-22).

title: Served round-2b model: D3_x3 + YAMNet + OPERA-CE + HeAR (production run #3)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
interpretation: Test split used for this configuration a second time (first: EXP-015, same configuration, superseded artifact); the configuration was fixed before (D-21), so nothing was chosen. Served files reproduce test_metrics.json exactly on the GPU; on the CPU 1 of 389 test recordings flips (TF32 near-tie), patient metrics identical.
limitations: In-cohort only. Split v3 differs from v2, so not comparable with EXP-012. 49 test patients (CI about ±12 points). KAUH in the test split: 3 patients.
justification: D-21 adoption; D-23/D-24 fixes.

title: Source-mixing mitigation on the KAUH holdout (round-2b served model)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
interpretation: 17/24 in-label holdout patients correct vs 0/24 for the model served before 2b (EXP-017): healthy 17/18 (exact CI 72.7–99.9%), COPD 0/5 (CI 0–52.2%), bronchial 0/1; balanced accuracy 31.5%. Out-of-label KAUH recordings moved from mostly 'asthma' to mostly 'healthy' (52/81): the model follows the site's dominant training label.
limitations: Within-site evaluation (KAUH patients in training), not cross-site. 24 in-label patients, 5 COPD. Holdout used twice for this configuration (once for EXP-015). 3 holdout healthy recordings are byte-identical to asthma recordings of training/validation patients (C-21); without them 18/24 (healthy 18/18, COPD 0/5) - backend/data/kauh_internal_duplicates.summary.json.
decision: H3 partly supported: criterion met on accuracy (+70.8 points), not on COPD or balanced accuracy
justification: Pre-registered in RESEARCH_PLAN H3 / ROUND2 report §9.

title: Abstention under site shift (all KAUH evaluations)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: abstention rate out-of-label − in-label (round-2b model, KAUH holdout)
secondary_metrics: {"EXP-011 pre-round-2 model, 45-patient external set": {"difference_ci95": [-0.0667, 0.2543], "in_label": 0.3259, "in_label_accuracy_accepted": 0.0, "in_label_accuracy_all": 0.0, "out_of_label": 0.4198}, "EXP-013 round-2 model, 45-patient external set": {"difference_ci95": [-0.0864, 0.242], "in_label": 0.3407, "in_label_accuracy_accepted": 0.0, "in_label_accuracy_all": 0.0, "out_of_label": 0.4198}, "EXP-017 round-2 model, 24-patient holdout": {"difference_ci95": [-0.1852, 0.1975], "in_label": 0.4167, "in_label_accuracy_accepted": 0.0, "in_label_accuracy_all": 0.0, "out_of_label": 0.4198}, "X3 round-2b model, 24-patient holdout": {"difference_ci95": [0.0278, 0.3364], "in_label": 0.4583, "in_label_accuracy_accepted": 0.7949, "in_label_accuracy_all": 0.6944, "out_of_label": 0.642}, "method": "patient-cluster bootstrap, 10000 draws, seed 0; recording-level rates"}
interpretation: Models without KAUH exposure abstain about as often on out-of-label as on in-label KAUH audio (CIs include 0) and pass most of their wrong external calls; after round 2b the difference is +18.4 points [2.8, 33.6].
limitations: Out-of-label = KAUH diagnoses outside the five classes, not other audio domains. Recording level with patient-cluster bootstrap; 24–45 in-label patients.
decision: H5 unsupported without site exposure; weakly supported after it
justification: Descriptive analysis planned in RESEARCH_PLAN (H5).

title: Fidelity grid: the 2020 protocol (L0) under its undocumented batch size and GRU gate
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
interpretation: The published code cannot run (undefined variables, no split/evaluation code). Under every plausible reading (batch 32 or full, sigmoid or Keras-2 hard sigmoid; 20 seeds each) the mean is 0.79–0.88 and none of 80 runs reaches the lowest of the paper's ten reported runs (0.949); keeping the best 10 of 20 adds about 2 points.
limitations: Re-implementation with minimal patches; librosa and Keras versions differ from 2020.
decision: 0.957 is not reproducible from the published materials
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.

title: Multiplicity control for the round-2b adoption (Holm)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: Holm-adjusted p of the adopted fusion (balanced accuracy, 4 pre-registered candidates)
interpretation: Raw one-sided bootstrap p 0.048 → 0.164 after Holm over the 4 pre-registered fusions (1.0 over all 35 reported); no candidate is significant after correction.
limitations: Bootstrap P(Δ>0) read as a one-sided p-value; 1,000 draws.
decision: adoption stands procedurally (rule fixed in advance); superiority over R′ is not claimed
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.

title: Normal vs abnormal AUROC: in cohort vs external KAUH
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: external AUROC, round-2 model (72 KAUH patients, no KAUH training data)
interpretation: Models without KAUH training data: AUROC 0.47-0.48 on 72 external KAUH patients (chance); in cohort the served model reaches 0.94 [0.87, 0.99] (test_prediction_analyses.json). After round 2b the KAUH holdout gives 0.83 (within site).
limitations: Patient-level; out-of-label KAUH diagnoses counted as abnormal; 18-35 normal patients.
decision: supports H2; comparable to Ong Ly et al. 2024 (0.97 -> 0.60)
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.

title: Leave-one-source-out, normal vs abnormal (dev patients)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: held-out-source AUROC, HeAR on the KAUH site
interpretation: Held out of training, each source drops to AUROC 0.38-0.59 in 10 of 12 representation x source cells (within-cohort 0.51-0.97). Leave-one-device-out is impossible: every healthy ICBHI recording is Meditron and the AKG C417L recorded only COPD.
limitations: Linear heads on frozen embeddings; development patients only; three sources.
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.

title: Source probes on non-breath audio
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: dataset-of-origin probe from the quietest 10% of frames
interpretation: The source stays decodable from the quietest frames (dataset 0.79, device 0.81, within-diagnosis 0.77-0.98) and the first/last 100 ms (0.76 / 0.83 / 0.72-0.96), close to the whole recording (0.86 / 0.83 / 0.88-1.00): an acquisition signature exists outside the breath sounds.
limitations: Quietest frames are not guaranteed breath-free; linear probes; shows the signature exists, not that models use it.
decision: 'acquisition signature that models can exploit' may be stated
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.

title: Served model test outputs: no-audio rule (paired), without Kaggle remainder
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: model − no-audio rule, patient balanced accuracy
interpretation: Model vs source+stethoscope rule: +4.1 points [-6.9, +16.1], P(model better) 0.77. Without the 6 Kaggle-remainder test patients: patient balanced accuracy 68.0% (74.9% with them).
limitations: CPU export (1 of 389 recordings differs from the GPU evaluation; patient metrics identical).
decision: in-cohort score not distinguishable from the no-audio rule
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.

title: Source-only baselines (no audio)
research_question: RQ1: leakage/shortcut share of reported accuracy; cross-site generalization
primary_metric: split v3: recording accuracy of the source+device rule
interpretation: Predicting the majority training label of each source and stethoscope reaches 84.1% recording accuracy on split v3 (served model 82.0%) and 70.8% patient balanced accuracy (model 74.9%). On X1 L3 the device rule (0.440 balanced) beats the 2020 network (0.384); the network is better in 7 of 20 paired seeds.
limitations: Rule fitted on train + validation; no confidence intervals for the merged-cohort comparison.
decision: supports H2: in-cohort scores largely reflect the source
justification: Tier-1 item of the readiness report.
